topic: Career angle: Goldman says losing a job to AI can leave a lasting scar. How to soften it before it happens.
post:
Losing a job to AI isn't just a gap on your résumé. 📉
Goldman Sachs research says it can leave a scar that lasts years.

What Goldman's economists found 👇
⏳ Workers displaced from tech-disrupted jobs took about a month longer to find a new one
📉 Many ended up in roles needing fewer skills. Goldman calls it "occupational downgrading"
💵 Over the following decade, their earnings grew noticeably slower than people who were never displaced

But here's the part that matters for your plan:
🎓 Younger, college-educated and urban workers saw losses roughly half as large
🔁 Goldman suggests retraining could soften the blow

In other words: the people who keep learning recover faster.

Why it matters:
The real risk isn't only losing a job. It's landing in a smaller one. Skills are what stop the downgrade. 🧭

Practical takeaway:
Don't wait for a layoff to retrain. Spend 30 minutes this week learning one AI skill that's used in the next role up from yours. 📚

What skill are you building right now? 👇
